hub.title: Quant interview
hub.lead: Timed sessions like a real interview: one question after another, no going back, then a scorecard and full solutions.
hub.ai: With AI grading when it's on

mental_math.title: Mental math
mental_math.description: 80 calculations in 8 minutes: addition, multiplication, division, percentages and fractions. Scored at once, with a personal best.

market_making.title: Market making
market_making.description: You quote a bid and an ask on an unknown quantity, such as the sum of three dice. A trader trades with you, and you see the result and the expected-value reasoning.

probability_sprint.title: Probability sprint
probability_sprint.description: 10 questions in 20 minutes, graded at once.

brainteasers.title: Brainteasers
brainteasers.description: Open questions with hints, as in an interview.

open_modelling.title: Modelling question
open_modelling.description: For example: how would you test whether this strategy has an edge?

setup.rulesMental: Type the result and press Enter. Fractions and percentages can be typed as 0.125, 1/8 or 12.5%. There is no going back to a previous calculation.
setup.rulesMarket: Each round, give a bid (what you'd buy at) and an ask (what you'd sell at). The trader roughly knows the value and trades when your price suits them.

market.crossed: The bid must be below the ask.
market.bought: The trader bought from you at {price}.
market.sold: The trader sold to you at {price}.
market.none: The trader didn't trade: your price didn't suit them.
market.evInside: The expected value is inside your quote (width {width}).
market.evOutside: The expected value is outside your quote, so a well-informed trader will win against you.
market.score: Quote score: {percent}%. P&L depends on the draw; the score only on your price.

three-dice.name: Sum of three dice
three-dice.how: Each die averages 3.5, so the sum of three averages 10.5.

ten-coins.name: Number of heads in 10 coin flips
ten-coins.how: Each flip is heads with probability 1/2, so on average 10 · 1/2 = 5.

max-two-dice.name: The larger of two dice
max-two-dice.how: P(max = k) = (2k − 1)/36, so the mean is 161/36 ≈ 4.47.

two-cards.name: Sum of two cards from ten (1–10), without replacement
two-cards.how: Each card averages 5.5, so the sum of two averages 11.

score.title: Scorecard
score.best: A new personal best at this level.

history.title: Session history
history.lead: Your sessions saved in this browser, and your progress in each type.
